claim: Over 500 genetic loci have been associated with risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs).
source: Over 500 genetic loci have been associated with risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs); however, most loci are located in gene-distal non-coding regions and their target genes are not known.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a factual assertion about the number of CVD-associated loci.

claim: Most CVD-associated loci are located in gene-distal non-coding regions.
source: Over 500 genetic loci have been associated with risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs); however, most loci are located in gene-distal non-coding regions and their target genes are not known.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a factual assertion about the location of CVD-associated loci.

claim: The target genes of most CVD-associated loci are not known.
source: Over 500 genetic loci have been associated with risk of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs); however, most loci are located in gene-distal non-coding regions and their target genes are not known.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a factual assertion about the unknown nature of target genes.

claim: High-resolution promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) maps were generated in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs).
source: Here, we generated high-resolution promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) maps in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) to provide a resource for identifying and prioritizing the functional targets of CVD associations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the experimental work performed.

claim: High-resolution promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) maps were generated in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs).
source: Here, we generated high-resolution promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) maps in human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) and iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (CMs) to provide a resource for identifying and prioritizing the functional targets of CVD associations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a description of the experimental work performed.

claim: Promoters preferentially contact distal sequences enriched for tissue-specific transcription factor motifs.
source: We validate these maps by demonstrating that promoters preferentially contact distal sequences enriched for tissue-specific transcription factor motifs and are enriched for chromatin marks that correlate with dynamic changes in gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a validation finding from the study.

claim: Promoter interactions are enriched for chromatin marks that correlate with dynamic changes in gene expression.
source: We validate these maps by demonstrating that promoters preferentially contact distal sequences enriched for tissue-specific transcription factor motifs and are enriched for chromatin marks that correlate with dynamic changes in gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a validation finding from the study.

claim: Using the CM PCHi-C map, 1999 CVD-associated SNPs were linked to 347 target genes.
source: Using the CM PCHi-C map, we linked 1999 CVD-associated SNPs to 347 target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a quantitative result from the study.

claim: More than 90% of SNP-target gene interactions did not involve the nearest gene.
source: Remarkably, more than 90% of SNP-target gene interactions did not involve the nearest gene, while 40% of SNPs interacted with at least two genes, demonstrating the importance of considering long-range chromatin interactions when interpreting functional targets of disease loci.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a quantitative finding from the study.

claim: 40% of CVD-associated SNPs interacted with at least two genes.
source: Remarkably, more than 90% of SNP-target gene interactions did not involve the nearest gene, while 40% of SNPs interacted with at least two genes, demonstrating the importance of considering long-range chromatin interactions when interpreting functional targets of disease loci.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a quantitative finding from the study.

claim: Most genome-wide association studies (GWAS) implicate non-coding variants that are far from genes.
source: Most genome-wide association studies (GWAS) implicate non-coding variants that are far from genes, complicating interpretation of their mode of action and correct identification of the target gene (Maurano et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Disease variants disrupt the function of cis-acting regulatory elements, such as enhancers.
source: Mounting evidence suggests that disease variants disrupt the function of cis-acting regulatory elements, such as enhancers, which in turn affects expression of the specific gene or genes that are functional targets of these elements (Wright et al., 2010; Musunuru et al., 2010; Cowper-Sal lari et al., 2012; Smemo et al., 2014; Claussnitzer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations supporting the claim.

claim: Cis-acting regulatory elements can be located kilobases away from their target gene(s).
source: However, because cis-acting regulatory elements can be located kilobases (kb) away from their target gene(s), identifying the true functional targets of regulatory elements remains challenging (Smemo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Hi-C enables the genome-wide mapping of long-range chromatin contacts.
source: Chromosome conformation capture techniques such as Hi-C (Lieberman-Aiden et al., 2009) enable the genome-wide mapping of long-range chromatin contacts and therefore represent a promising strategy to identify distal gene targets of disease-associated genetic variants.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Hi-C maps have been generated in numerous human cell types including embryonic stem cells and early embryonic lineages.
source: Recently, Hi-C maps have been generated in numerous human cell types including embryonic stem cells and early embryonic lineages (Dixon et al., 2012, 2015), immune cells (Rao et al., 2014), fibroblasts (Jin et al., 2013) and other primary tissue types (Schmitt et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Most Hi-C datasets are of limited resolution (>40 kb).
source: However, despite the increasing abundance of Hi-C maps, most datasets are of limited resolution (>40 kb) and do not precisely identify the genomic regions in contact with gene promoters.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of existing Hi-C datasets.

claim: Promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) greatly increases the power to detect interactions involving promoter sequences.
source: More recently, promoter capture Hi-C (PCHi-C) was developed which greatly increases the power to detect interactions involving promoter sequences (Schoenfelder et al., 2015; Mifsud et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: PCHi-C in different cell types identified thousands of enhancer-promoter contacts.
source: PCHi-C in different cell types identified thousands of enhancer-promoter contacts and revealed extensive differences in promoter architecture between cell types and throughout differentiation (Schoenfelder et al., 2015; Mifsud et al., 2015; Javierre et al., 2016; Freire-Pritchett et al., 2017; Rubin et al., 2017; Siersbæk et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Genome architecture reflects cell identity.
source: These studies collectively demonstrated that genome architecture reflects cell identity, suggesting that disease-relevant cell types are critical for successful interrogation of the gene regulatory mechanisms of disease loci.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from previous studies.

claim: Javierre et al. generated promoter capture Hi-C data in 17 primary human blood cell types.
source: Javierre et al. generated promoter capture Hi-C data in 17 primary human blood cell types and identified 2604 potentially causal genes for immune- and blood-related disorders, including many genes with unannotated roles in those diseases (Javierre et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Javierre et al. identified 2604 potentially causal genes for immune- and blood-related disorders.
source: Javierre et al. generated promoter capture Hi-C data in 17 primary human blood cell types and identified 2604 potentially causal genes for immune- and blood-related disorders, including many genes with unannotated roles in those diseases (Javierre et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Mumbach et al. identified ~10,000 promoter-enhancer interactions using HiChIP.
source: Similarly, Mumbach et al. interrogated GWAS SNPs associated with autoimmune diseases using HiChIP where they identified ~10,000 promoter-enhancer interactions that linked several hundred SNPs to target genes, most of which were not the nearest gene (Mumbach et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: SNP-target gene interactions are cell-type specific.
source: Importantly, both studies reported cell-type specificity of SNP-target gene interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous studies.

claim: Cardiovascular diseases continue to be the leading cause of death world-wide.
source: Cardiovascular diseases, including cardiac arrhythmia, heart failure, and myocardial infarction, continue to be the leading cause of death world-wide.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a factual assertion.

claim: Over 50 GWAS have been conducted for cardiovascular phenotypes.
source: Over 50 GWAS have been conducted for these specific cardiovascular phenotypes alone, with more than 500 loci implicated in cardiovascular disease risk (NHGRI GWAS catalog, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/), most of which map to non-coding genomic regions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a reference to the NHGRI GWAS catalog.

claim: More than 500 loci are implicated in cardiovascular disease risk.
source: Over 50 GWAS have been conducted for these specific cardiovascular phenotypes alone, with more than 500 loci implicated in cardiovascular disease risk (NHGRI GWAS catalog, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/), most of which map to non-coding genomic regions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a reference to the NHGRI GWAS catalog.

claim: Most CVD-associated loci map to non-coding genomic regions.
source: Over 50 GWAS have been conducted for these specific cardiovascular phenotypes alone, with more than 500 loci implicated in cardiovascular disease risk (NHGRI GWAS catalog, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/), most of which map to non-coding genomic regions.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a reference to the NHGRI GWAS catalog.

claim: The CMs generated in this study were 86–94% pure based on cardiac Troponin T protein expression.
source: The CMs generated in this study were 86–94% pure based on cardiac Troponin T protein expression and exhibited spontaneous, uniform beating (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing flow cytometry data.

claim: iPSC-derived CMs exhibited spontaneous, uniform beating.
source: The CMs generated in this study were 86–94% pure based on cardiac Troponin T protein expression and exhibited spontaneous, uniform beating (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a video showing beating cells.

claim: RNA-seq profiles of iPSCs clustered tightly with H1 embryonic stem cells.
source: RNA-seq profiles of iPSCs clustered tightly with H1 embryonic stem cells, whereas CMs clustered with both left ventricle (LV) and fetal heart (FH) profiles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing PCA analysis.

claim: RNA-seq profiles of CMs clustered with both left ventricle (LV) and fetal heart (FH) profiles.
source: RNA-seq profiles of iPSCs clustered tightly with H1 embryonic stem cells, whereas CMs clustered with both left ventricle (LV) and fetal heart (FH) profiles (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing PCA analysis.

claim: Matched cell types exhibited three-fold greater overlap in the number of promoter-distal H3K27ac ChIP-seq peaks than non-matched cell types.
source: Furthermore, we observed that matched cell types exhibited three-fold greater overlap in the number of promoter-distal H3K27ac ChIP-seq peaks than non-matched cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D), indicating that both iPSCs and CMs recapitulate tissue-specific epigenetic states of human stem cells and primary cardiomyocytes, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing ChIP-seq peak overlap.

claim: iPSCs and CMs recapitulate tissue-specific epigenetic states of human stem cells and primary cardiomyocytes, respectively.
source: Furthermore, we observed that matched cell types exhibited three-fold greater overlap in the number of promoter-distal H3K27ac ChIP-seq peaks than non-matched cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D), indicating that both iPSCs and CMs recapitulate tissue-specific epigenetic states of human stem cells and primary cardiomyocytes, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the ChIP-seq data.

claim: Among the top 10% of over-expressed genes in CMs were genes directly related to cardiac function including essential cardiac transcription factors (GATA4, MEIS1, TBX5, and TBX20).
source: Among the top 10% of over-expressed genes in CMs were genes directly related to cardiac function including essential cardiac transcription factors (GATA4, MEIS1, TBX5, and TBX20) and differentiation products (TNNT2, MYH7B, MYL7, ACTN2, NPPA, HCN4, and RYR2) (fold-change >1.5, Padj <0.05, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing differential expression analysis.

claim: Among the top 10% of over-expressed genes in CMs were differentiation products (TNNT2, MYH7B, MYL7, ACTN2, NPPA, HCN4, and RYR2).
source: Among the top 10% of over-expressed genes in CMs were genes directly related to cardiac function including essential cardiac transcription factors (GATA4, MEIS1, TBX5, and TBX20) and differentiation products (TNNT2, MYH7B, MYL7, ACTN2, NPPA, HCN4, and RYR2) (fold-change >1.5, Padj <0.05, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing differential expression analysis.

claim: Gene Ontology enrichment analysis for genes over-expressed in CMs relative to iPSCs revealed top terms relating to the development of the cardiac conduction system and cardiac muscle cell contraction.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis for genes over-expressed in CMs relative to iPSCs further confirmed the cardiac-specific phenotypes of these cells with top terms relating to the development of the cardiac conduction system and cardiac muscle cell contraction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: In-situ Hi-C was performed in triplicate iPSC-CM differentiations.
source: To comprehensively map long-range regulatory elements in iPSCs and CMs, we performed in-situ Hi-C (Rao et al., 2014) in triplicate iPSC-CM differentiations; importantly, we used the four-cutter restriction enzyme MboI which generates ligation fragments with an average size of 422 bp, enabling enhancer-level resolution of promoter contacts.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the experimental design.

claim: The four-cutter restriction enzyme MboI generates ligation fragments with an average size of 422 bp.
source: To comprehensively map long-range regulatory elements in iPSCs and CMs, we performed in-situ Hi-C (Rao et al., 2014) in triplicate iPSC-CM differentiations; importantly, we used the four-cutter restriction enzyme MboI which generates ligation fragments with an average size of 422 bp, enabling enhancer-level resolution of promoter contacts.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the experimental method.

claim: iPSC and CM in situ Hi-C libraries were enriched for promoter interactions through hybridization with a set of 77,476 biotinylated RNA probes targeting 22,600 human RefSeq protein-coding promoters.
source: We enriched iPSC and CM in situ Hi-C libraries for promoter interactions through hybridization with a set of 77,476 biotinylated RNA probes ('baits') targeting 22,600 human RefSeq protein-coding promoters (see Materials and methods) and sequenced each library to an average depth of ~413 million (M) paired-end reads.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the experimental method.

claim: Each Hi-C library was sequenced to an average depth of ~413 million paired-end reads.
source: We enriched iPSC and CM in situ Hi-C libraries for promoter interactions through hybridization with a set of 77,476 biotinylated RNA probes ('baits') targeting 22,600 human RefSeq protein-coding promoters (see Materials and methods) and sequenced each library to an average depth of ~413 million (M) paired-end reads.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the sequencing depth.

claim: An average of 31M read-pairs per replicate were obtained for iPSC after removing duplicates and read-pairs that did not map to a bait.
source: After removing duplicates and read-pairs that did not map to a bait, we obtained an average of 31M and 41M read-pairs per replicate for iPSC and CM, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the data processing.

claim: An average of 41M read-pairs per replicate were obtained for CM after removing duplicates and read-pairs that did not map to a bait.
source: After removing duplicates and read-pairs that did not map to a bait, we obtained an average of 31M and 41M read-pairs per replicate for iPSC and CM, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the data processing.

claim: CHiCAGO was used to identify significant interactions.
source: We used CHiCAGO (Cairns et al., 2016), a computational pipeline which accounts for bias from the sequence capture, to identify significant interactions and further filtered for those significant in at least two out of three replicates (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the computational method.

claim: Interactions were filtered for those significant in at least two out of three replicates.
source: We used CHiCAGO (Cairns et al., 2016), a computational pipeline which accounts for bias from the sequence capture, to identify significant interactions and further filtered for those significant in at least two out of three replicates (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the filtering criteria.

claim: Only interactions separated by a distance of at least 10 kb were analyzed.
source: Finally, we exclusively focused on interactions that were separated by a distance of at least 10 kb.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the filtering criteria.

claim: 350,062 promoter interactions were identified in iPSCs.
source: In total, we identified 350,062 promoter interactions in iPSCs and 401,098 in CMs.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a quantitative finding from the study.

claim: 401,098 promoter interactions were identified in CMs.
source: In total, we identified 350,062 promoter interactions in iPSCs and 401,098 in CMs.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a quantitative finding from the study.

claim: Approximately 55% of promoter interactions were shared between iPSCs and CMs.
source: A large proportion (~55%) of interactions were shared between the two cell types, indicating that even at high resolution many long-range interactions are stable across cell types (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the overlap of interactions.

claim: Approximately 20% of all interactions were between two promoters.
source: Approximately 20% of all interactions were between two promoters, demonstrating the high connectivity between genes and supporting the recently suggested role of promoters acting as regulatory inputs for distal genes (Dao et al., 2017; Diao et al., 2017) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the proportion of interaction types.

claim: Most promoter interactions were promoter-distal, with a median of ~170 kb between the promoter and the distal-interacting region.
source: Most interactions were promoter-distal, with a median of ~170 kb between the promoter and the distal-interacting region (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the distribution of interaction distances.

claim: The majority of PCHi-C interactions occurred within TADs (73% in iPSCs and 77% in CMs).
source: We found that the majority of PCHi-C interactions occurred within TADs (73 and 77% in iPSCs and CMs, respectively; Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: TAD-crossing interactions ('inter-TAD') contained proportionally more promoter-promoter interactions than intra-TAD interactions.
source: TAD-crossing interactions ('inter-TAD') contained proportionally more promoter-promoter interactions than intra-TAD interactions, and were more likely to overlap promoter-distal CTCF sites; however, they were similarly enriched for looping to distal H3K27ac sites, a mark of active chromatin (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Inter-TAD interactions were more likely to overlap promoter-distal CTCF sites than intra-TAD interactions.
source: TAD-crossing interactions ('inter-TAD') contained proportionally more promoter-promoter interactions than intra-TAD interactions, and were more likely to overlap promoter-distal CTCF sites; however, they were similarly enriched for looping to distal H3K27ac sites, a mark of active chromatin (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Inter-TAD interactions were similarly enriched for looping to distal H3K27ac sites as intra-TAD interactions.
source: TAD-crossing interactions ('inter-TAD') contained proportionally more promoter-promoter interactions than intra-TAD interactions, and were more likely to overlap promoter-distal CTCF sites; however, they were similarly enriched for looping to distal H3K27ac sites, a mark of active chromatin (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Inter-TAD interactions had slightly lower CHiCAGO scores than intra-TAD interactions.
source: Inter-TAD interactions had slightly lower CHiCAGO scores, reflecting a lower number of reads supporting these interactions, and spanned greater genomic distances than intra-TAD interactions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Inter-TAD interactions spanned greater genomic distances than intra-TAD interactions.
source: Inter-TAD interactions had slightly lower CHiCAGO scores, reflecting a lower number of reads supporting these interactions, and spanned greater genomic distances than intra-TAD interactions (Figure 1—figure supplement 3E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Promoters with inter-TAD interactions were preferentially located close to TAD boundaries.
source: Additionally, promoters with inter-TAD interactions were preferentially located close to TAD boundaries (Figure 1—figure supplement 3G) and had higher expression levels compared to promoters with intra-TAD interactions, particularly in CMs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Promoters with inter-TAD interactions had higher expression levels compared to promoters with intra-TAD interactions, particularly in CMs.
source: Additionally, promoters with inter-TAD interactions were preferentially located close to TAD boundaries (Figure 1—figure supplement 3G) and had higher expression levels compared to promoters with intra-TAD interactions, particularly in CMs (Figure 1—figure supplement 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing TAD analysis.

claim: Highly expressed genes are enriched at TAD boundaries.
source: These observations are consistent with previous studies which demonstrated that highly expressed genes, specifically housekeeping genes, are enriched at TAD boundaries (Dixon et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: PCHi-C identified increased interaction frequencies between the GATA4 promoter and several H3K27ac-marked regions in CMs.
source: However, PCHi-C identified increased interaction frequencies between the GATA4 promoter and several H3K27ac-marked regions, including four in vivo validated heart enhancers from the Vista enhancer browser (Visel et al., 2007), specifically in CMs and coincident with strong up-regulation of GATA4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the GATA4 locus.

claim: The GATA4 promoter interacts with four in vivo validated heart enhancers in CMs.
source: However, PCHi-C identified increased interaction frequencies between the GATA4 promoter and several H3K27ac-marked regions, including four in vivo validated heart enhancers from the Vista enhancer browser (Visel et al., 2007), specifically in CMs and coincident with strong up-regulation of GATA4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the GATA4 locus and a citation to the Vista enhancer browser.

claim: CTCF was identified as the most enriched motif in promoter-distal interacting sequences in both iPSCs and CMs.
source: We identified CTCF as the most enriched motif in each case (Figure 2A,B), consistent with the known role of this factor in mediating long-range genomic interactions (Phillips and Corces, 2009; Phillips-Cremins et al., 2013; Nora et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing motif analysis.

claim: The pluripotency factor motifs OCT4-SOX2-TCF-NANOG (OSN) and SOX2 were preferentially enriched in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in iPSCs.
source: Among the other top motifs, we identified the pluripotency factor motifs OCT4-SOX2-TCF-NANOG (OSN) and SOX2 as preferentially enriched in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in iPSCs (Figure 2A,C), whereas top motifs in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in CMs included TBX20, ESRRB and MEIS1 (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing motif analysis.

claim: Top motifs in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in CMs included TBX20, ESRRB and MEIS1.
source: Among the other top motifs, we identified the pluripotency factor motifs OCT4-SOX2-TCF-NANOG (OSN) and SOX2 as preferentially enriched in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in iPSCs (Figure 2A,C), whereas top motifs in distal sequences looping to genes over-expressed in CMs included TBX20, ESRRB and MEIS1 (Figure 2B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing motif analysis.

claim: TBX20 and MEIS1 transcription factors are important regulators of heart development and function.
source: TBX20 and MEIS1 transcription factors are important regulators of heart development and function (Cai et al., 2005; Sakabe et al., 2012; Mahmoud et al., 2013) and ESRRB was previously identified as a potential binding partner of TBX20 in adult mouse cardiomyocytes (Shen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations supporting the claim.

claim: ESRRB was previously identified as a potential binding partner of TBX20 in adult mouse cardiomyocytes.
source: TBX20 and MEIS1 transcription factors are important regulators of heart development and function (Cai et al., 2005; Sakabe et al., 2012; Mahmoud et al., 2013) and ESRRB was previously identified as a potential binding partner of TBX20 in adult mouse cardiomyocytes (Shen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Both iPSC- and CM-specific interactions were enriched for AP-1 motifs.
source: In line with a recent report that AP-1 contributes to dynamic loop formation during macrophage development (Phanstiel et al., 2017), both iPSC- and CM-specific interactions were enriched for AP-1 motifs (Figure 2D), suggesting that AP-1 transcription factors may represent a previously unrecognized genome organizing complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing motif analysis.

claim: AP-1 transcription factors may represent a previously unrecognized genome organizing complex.
source: In line with a recent report that AP-1 contributes to dynamic loop formation during macrophage development (Phanstiel et al., 2017), both iPSC- and CM-specific interactions were enriched for AP-1 motifs (Figure 2D), suggesting that AP-1 transcription factors may represent a previously unrecognized genome organizing complex.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a speculation based on the motif enrichment data.

claim: Promoter-distal MboI fragments involved in significant promoter interactions were enriched for H3K4me1, H3K27ac, and H3K27me3 in both iPSCs and CMs.
source: In support of the gene-regulatory function of long-range interactions, we found that the promoter-distal MboI fragments involved in significant promoter interactions were enriched for these three histone modifications in both iPSCs and CMs (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing histone modification enrichment.

claim: Enrichment for H3K27ac and H3K4me1 increased with increasing promoter expression level.
source: When promoters were grouped by expression level, we observed that this enrichment increased with increasing expression for H3K27ac and H3K4me1, and decreased with increasing expression for H3K27me3, consistent with an additive nature of enhancer-promoter interactions (Schoenfelder et al., 2015; Javierre et al., 2016), and validating that PCHi-C enriches for likely functional long-range chromatin contacts.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing histone modification enrichment by expression level.

claim: Enrichment for H3K27me3 decreased with increasing promoter expression level.
source: When promoters were grouped by expression level, we observed that this enrichment increased with increasing expression for H3K27ac and H3K4me1, and decreased with increasing expression for H3K27me3, consistent with an additive nature of enhancer-promoter interactions (Schoenfelder et al., 2015; Javierre et al., 2016), and validating that PCHi-C enriches for likely functional long-range chromatin contacts.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing histone modification enrichment by expression level.

claim: H3K27ac and H3K4me1 positively correlated with promoter expression level (Spearman's ρ = 0.22 and 0.16, respectively in iPSC and ρ = 0.23 and 0.24, respectively in CMs, p<2.2−16).
source: H3K27ac and H3K4me1 both positively correlated with expression level (Spearman's ρ = 0.22 and 0.16, respectively in iPSC and ρ = 0.23 and 0.24, respectively in CMs, p<2.2−16); in contrast, H3K27me3 negatively correlated with expression level in CMs (Spearman's ρ = −0.20, p<2.2−16); however, this relationship was not present in iPSCs (Spearman's ρ = 0.02, p=0.06).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing correlation analysis.

claim: H3K27me3 negatively correlated with expression level in CMs (Spearman's ρ = −0.20, p<2.2−16).
source: H3K27ac and H3K4me1 both positively correlated with expression level (Spearman's ρ = 0.22 and 0.16, respectively in iPSC and ρ = 0.23 and 0.24, respectively in CMs, p<2.2−16); in contrast, H3K27me3 negatively correlated with expression level in CMs (Spearman's ρ = −0.20, p<2.2−16); however, this relationship was not present in iPSCs (Spearman's ρ = 0.02, p=0.06).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing correlation analysis.

claim: H3K27me3 did not correlate with expression level in iPSCs (Spearman's ρ = 0.02, p=0.06).
source: H3K27ac and H3K4me1 both positively correlated with expression level (Spearman's ρ = 0.22 and 0.16, respectively in iPSC and ρ = 0.23 and 0.24, respectively in CMs, p<2.2−16); in contrast, H3K27me3 negatively correlated with expression level in CMs (Spearman's ρ = −0.20, p<2.2−16); however, this relationship was not present in iPSCs (Spearman's ρ = 0.02, p=0.06).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing correlation analysis.

claim: Cell-type-specific interactions preferentially involved H3K27ac peaks from the matched cell type.
source: Indeed, we observed that cell-type-specific interactions preferentially involved H3K27ac peaks from the matched cell type, and were either not enriched (iPSC) or depleted (CM) for H3K27ac marks that were specific to the non-matched cell type (Figure 3E, middle panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing enrichment analysis.

claim: Cell-type-specific interactions were either not enriched (iPSC) or depleted (CM) for H3K27ac marks that were specific to the non-matched cell type.
source: Indeed, we observed that cell-type-specific interactions preferentially involved H3K27ac peaks from the matched cell type, and were either not enriched (iPSC) or depleted (CM) for H3K27ac marks that were specific to the non-matched cell type (Figure 3E, middle panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing enrichment analysis.

claim: The strongest enrichment was for cell-type-specific interactions to overlap chromatin features that were present in both cell types.
source: However, the strongest enrichment was for cell-type-specific interactions to overlap chromatin features that were present in both cell types (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing enrichment analysis.

claim: Interactions that were shared between iPSCs and CMs were most enriched for shared chromatin features.
source: Additionally, interactions that were shared between iPSCs and CMs were most enriched for shared chromatin features.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a finding from the enrichment analysis.

claim: NPPA is specifically expressed in cells of the heart atrium.
source: An example of a gene that encompasses these observations is the atrial natriuretic peptide gene NPPA (Figure 3F) which is specifically expressed in cells of the heart atrium and is upregulated in CMs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the NPPA locus.

claim: NPPA is upregulated in CMs.
source: An example of a gene that encompasses these observations is the atrial natriuretic peptide gene NPPA (Figure 3F) which is specifically expressed in cells of the heart atrium and is upregulated in CMs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the NPPA locus.

claim: NPPA makes numerous cell-type-specific interactions to a distal region that is only marked with active chromatin (H3K27ac and H3K4me1) in CMs.
source: NPPA makes numerous cell-type-specific interactions to a distal region that is only marked with active chromatin (H3K27ac and H3K4me1) in CMs; furthermore, functional characterization showed that this region corresponds to an in vivo enhancer recapitulating NPPA's endogenous expression in the developing heart (Visel et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the NPPA locus.

claim: The distal region interacting with NPPA corresponds to an in vivo enhancer recapitulating NPPA's endogenous expression in the developing heart.
source: NPPA makes numerous cell-type-specific interactions to a distal region that is only marked with active chromatin (H3K27ac and H3K4me1) in CMs; furthermore, functional characterization showed that this region corresponds to an in vivo enhancer recapitulating NPPA's endogenous expression in the developing heart (Visel et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: The genome is organized in two major compartments, A and B, that correspond to open and closed regions of chromosomes, respectively.
source: The first Hi-C studies revealed that the genome is organized in two major compartments, A and B, that correspond to open and closed regions of chromosomes, respectively (Lieberman-Aiden et al., 2009; Rao et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Most compartments are stable across different cell types.
source: Although most compartments are stable across different cell types, some compartments switch states in a cell-type-specific manner which may reflect important gene regulatory changes (Dixon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Some compartments switch states in a cell-type-specific manner which may reflect important gene regulatory changes.
source: Although most compartments are stable across different cell types, some compartments switch states in a cell-type-specific manner which may reflect important gene regulatory changes (Dixon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: A/B compartments identified using HOMER were remarkably similar in the whole-genome and PCHi-C datasets (97% correspondence).
source: A/B compartments identified using HOMER (Heinz et al., 2010) were remarkably similar in the whole-genome and PCHi-C datasets (97% correspondence, Figure 4A, top panel, and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2), demonstrating that PCHi-C data contains sufficient information to identify broadly active and inactive regions of the genome.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing A/B compartment analysis.

claim: PCHi-C data contains sufficient information to identify broadly active and inactive regions of the genome.
source: A/B compartments identified using HOMER (Heinz et al., 2010) were remarkably similar in the whole-genome and PCHi-C datasets (97% correspondence, Figure 4A, top panel, and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2), demonstrating that PCHi-C data contains sufficient information to identify broadly active and inactive regions of the genome.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the A/B compartment analysis.

claim: The CAMK2D gene was located in a dynamic compartment that switched from inactive in iPSCs to active in CMs.
source: Compartments were relatively stable across this region in iPSCs and CMs; however, the CAMK2D gene itself was located in a dynamic compartment that switched from inactive in iPSCs to active in CMs.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the CAMK2D locus.

claim: CAMK2D was highly upregulated during differentiation to CMs.
source: Correspondingly, this gene was highly upregulated during differentiation to CMs (Figure 4A, inset).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the CAMK2D locus.

claim: Genes located in A compartments were expressed at significantly higher levels than genes located in the B compartments in both iPSCs and CMs.
source: We observed this effect on a global level, as genes located in A compartments were expressed at significantly higher levels than genes located in the B compartments in both iPSCs and CMs (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing expression levels by compartment.

claim: Genes that switched A/B compartments between cell types were correspondingly up- or down-regulated.
source: Additionally, genes that switched A/B compartments between cell types were correspondingly up- or down-regulated (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing expression changes by compartment switching.

claim: GO analysis of the 1008 genes that switched from B to A compartments during iPSC-CM differentiation revealed enrichment for terms such as 'cardiovascular system development' and 'heart contraction'.
source: GO analysis of the 1008 genes that switched from B to A compartments during iPSC-CM differentiation revealed enrichment for terms such as 'cardiovascular system development' and 'heart contraction' (Figure 4D, Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: GO analysis for genes that switched from A to B compartments during iPSC-CM differentiation related to non-cardiac processes, such as skin development, epithelial cell differentiation and sex determination.
source: GO analysis for genes that switched from A to B compartments during iPSC-CM differentiation related to non-cardiac processes, such as skin development, epithelial cell differentiation and sex determination (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 5 and 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: Compartmentalization of genes in spatially regulated regions of the nucleus may be one mechanism to ensure tissue-specific gene expression.
source: These data show that PCHi-C accurately captured tissue-specific interactions and indicate that compartmentalization of genes in spatially regulated regions of the nucleus may be one mechanism to ensure tissue-specific gene expression (Dixon et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the compartment analysis with a citation.

claim: 524 lead SNPs were compiled from the NHGRI database for three important classes of CVDs: cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and myocardial infarction.
source: We compiled 524 lead SNPs from the NHGRI database (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/) for three important classes of CVDs: cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, and myocardial infarction (Table 1, Supplementary files 7 and 8).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the GWAS SNP compilation.

claim: The set of lead SNPs was expanded to include all variants in high LD (r2 >0.9, within 50 kb of lead SNP), increasing the number of putatively causal variants to 10,475.
source: Because of linkage disequilibrium (LD) patterns, the true causal SNP could be any SNP in high LD with the lead variant. Therefore, we expanded this set of SNPs to include all variants in high LD (r2 >0.9, within 50 kb of lead SNP), increasing the number of putatively causal variants to 10,475 (hereafter called LD SNPs).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a description of the LD SNP expansion.

claim: 1999 (19%) of the LD SNPs were located in promoter-distal MboI fragments that interacted with the promoters of 347 genes in CMs.
source: We found that 1999 (19%) of the LD SNPs were located in promoter-distal MboI fragments that interacted with the promoters of 347 genes in CMs (Supplementary file 8), hereafter referred to as target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a quantitative finding from the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: The majority (89%) of LD SNP-target gene pairs were located within the same TAD.
source: The majority (89%) of LD SNP-target gene pairs were located within the same TAD, with a median distance of 185 kb between each SNP-target gene pair (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the distribution of SNP-target gene distances.

claim: The median distance between each SNP-target gene pair was 185 kb.
source: The majority (89%) of LD SNP-target gene pairs were located within the same TAD, with a median distance of 185 kb between each SNP-target gene pair (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the distribution of SNP-target gene distances.

claim: 90.4% of SNP-target gene interactions skipped at least one gene promoter.
source: Importantly, 90.4% of SNP-target gene interactions skipped at least one gene promoter and 42% of SNPs interacted with at least two different promoters (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the number of TSS's skipped.

claim: 42% of SNPs interacted with at least two different promoters.
source: Importantly, 90.4% of SNP-target gene interactions skipped at least one gene promoter and 42% of SNPs interacted with at least two different promoters (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the number of genes contacted by each SNP.

claim: Target genes were highly and specifically enriched for biological processes related to cardiac function, such as membrane repolarization and cardiac conduction.
source: To confirm that the CM PCHi-C interactions linked SNPs to CVD-relevant target genes, we performed GO analysis and found that target genes were highly and specifically enriched for biological processes related to cardiac function, such as membrane repolarization and cardiac conduction (Figure 5C, left panel and Supplementary file 5 and 6).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: A statistically significant number of target genes resulted in a cardiovascular phenotype when knocked-out in the mouse (78 genes (22.4%), p=1 × 10−5).
source: To further characterize the biological relevance of target genes, we mined mouse knock-out data from the Mouse Genome Informatics (MGI) database (Blake et al., 2017), which revealed that a statistically significant number of target genes resulted in a cardiovascular phenotype when knocked-out in the mouse (78 genes (22.4%), p=1 × 10−5, Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing MGI analysis.

claim: Of the 1999 LD SNPs in interactions, 410 (20.5%) corresponded to LV eQTLs.
source: Finally, we examined expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data from human left ventricle (LV) tissue obtained as part of the Genotype-Tissue Expresion (GTEx) Project (Carithers et al., 2015) and found that of the 1999 LD SNPs in interactions, 410 (20.5%) corresponded to LV eQTLs; in comparison, only 12.2% of the full set of LD SNPs corresponded to LV eQTLs (p<0.00001, Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing eQTL analysis.

claim: Only 12.2% of the full set of LD SNPs corresponded to LV eQTLs.
source: Finally, we examined expression quantitative trait loci (eQTL) data from human left ventricle (LV) tissue obtained as part of the Genotype-Tissue Expresion (GTEx) Project (Carithers et al., 2015) and found that of the 1999 LD SNPs in interactions, 410 (20.5%) corresponded to LV eQTLs; in comparison, only 12.2% of the full set of LD SNPs corresponded to LV eQTLs (p<0.00001, Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing eQTL analysis.

claim: On a genome-wide level, LV eQTLs in promoter-distal interactions were significantly more likely to loop to their associated gene than expected by chance (p<0.00001).
source: On a genome-wide level, LV eQTLs in promoter-distal interactions were significantly more likely to loop to their associated gene than expected by chance (p<0.00001, Figure 5F, left panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing eQTL analysis.

claim: The significance of LV eQTLs looping to their associated gene decreased when LV eQTLs were analyzed with iPSC promoter interactions (p=0.035).
source: Importantly, this significance decreased when LV eQTLs were analyzed with iPSC promoter interactions (p=0.035, Figure 5F, right panel).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing eQTL analysis.

claim: CM promoter interactions identify a subset of disease-relevant SNPs most likely to be functional.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that CM promoter interactions identify a subset of disease-relevant SNPs most likely to be functional and support the use of the CM map to assign distal CVD-associated SNPs to putative target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: Target genes were moderately over-expressed in CMs compared to iPSCs (median log2 fold change = 1.08, mean log2 fold change = 1.44, mean TPM values were 40.6 in iPSCs and 60.1 in CMs, p=0.12).
source: We examined the expression level of the 347 target genes and found that they were moderately over-expressed in CMs compared to iPSCs (median log2 fold change = 1.08, mean log2 fold change = 1.44, mean TPM values were 40.6 in iPSCs and 60.1 in CMs, p=0.12, Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing expression analysis.

claim: 21 of the 78 target genes (27%) that cause cardiovascular phenotypes when knocked-out in mice were overexpressed in iPSCs compared to CMs.
source: Indeed, we found that 21 of the 78 target genes (27%) that cause cardiovascular phenotypes when knocked-out in mice were overexpressed in iPSCs compared to CMs (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is stated in the results as a quantitative finding from the expression analysis.

claim: Gene expression level alone may be an insufficient metric to gauge the relevance of target genes to CVD biology.
source: However, because a subset of target genes was over-expressed in iPSCs relative to CMs (Figure 6C), we predicted that gene expression level alone may be an insufficient metric to gauge the relevance of target genes to CVD biology.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the expression analysis.

claim: Putatively causal genes may not appear as obvious candidates based solely on gene expression data.
source: This result indicates that putatively causal genes may not appear as obvious candidates based solely on gene expression data.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the expression analysis.

claim: The TBX5 gene formed long-range interactions to LD SNPs identified in arrhythmia GWAS.
source: To illustrate this point, we highlight two genes: TBX5, a gene directly linked to cardiac arrhythmia (Figure 6D) (Smemo et al., 2012; Arnolds et al., 2012), and LITAF, a gene that, until recently, had no obvious role in cardiac biology (Moshal et al., 2017) (Figure 6E). Both genes formed long-range interactions to LD SNPs identified in arrhythmia GWAS, making both genes candidate functional targets of the GWAS associations.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the TBX5 locus.

claim: The LITAF gene formed long-range interactions to LD SNPs identified in arrhythmia GWAS.
source: To illustrate this point, we highlight two genes: TBX5, a gene directly linked to cardiac arrhythmia (Figure 6D) (Smemo et al., 2012; Arnolds et al., 2012), and LITAF, a gene that, until recently, had no obvious role in cardiac biology (Moshal et al., 2017) (Figure 6E). Both genes formed long-range interactions to LD SNPs identified in arrhythmia GWAS, making both genes candidate functional targets of the GWAS associations.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to figures showing the LITAF locus.

claim: TBX5 is a gene directly linked to cardiac arrhythmia.
source: To illustrate this point, we highlight two genes: TBX5, a gene directly linked to cardiac arrhythmia (Figure 6D) (Smemo et al., 2012; Arnolds et al., 2012), and LITAF, a gene that, until recently, had no obvious role in cardiac biology (Moshal et al., 2017) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations supporting the claim.

claim: LITAF, until recently, had no obvious role in cardiac biology.
source: To illustrate this point, we highlight two genes: TBX5, a gene directly linked to cardiac arrhythmia (Figure 6D) (Smemo et al., 2012; Arnolds et al., 2012), and LITAF, a gene that, until recently, had no obvious role in cardiac biology (Moshal et al., 2017) (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: A recent study identified LITAF as a regulator of cardiac excitation in zebrafish hearts.
source: LITAF, on the other hand, was over-expressed in iPSCs compared to CMs (Figure 6C) and was not known to contribute to cardiac function until a recent study identified this gene as a regulator of cardiac excitation in zebrafish hearts (Moshal et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: The majority of the GO enrichment for cardiac terms was driven by the cardiac arrhythmia SNPs.
source: When broken down into the respective disease classes, we confirmed that the majority of the GO enrichment for cardiac terms was driven by the cardiac arrhythmia SNPs (Figure 7A), with terms directly related to the cardiac conduction system.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: Myocardial infarction analyses uncovered a set of genes that were slightly enriched for regulation of growth.
source: Myocardial infarction (Figure 7B) and heart failure (Figure 7C) analyses uncovered a set of genes that were slightly enriched for regulation of growth and morphogenesis, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: Heart failure analyses uncovered a set of genes that were slightly enriched for morphogenesis.
source: Myocardial infarction (Figure 7B) and heart failure (Figure 7C) analyses uncovered a set of genes that were slightly enriched for regulation of growth and morphogenesis, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing GO analysis.

claim: A careful screen of genes whose expression was affected by the risk allele at the 1p13 locus implicated the more distal SORT1 gene.
source: For example, one of the strongest associations for myocardial infarction lies in-between the CELSR2 and PSRC1 genes on chromosome 1p13, but a careful screen of genes whose expression was affected by the risk allele implicated the more distal SORT1 gene (Musunuru et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: SORT1 encodes a sorting receptor that is expressed in many tissues and has been shown to act in the liver to regulate cholesterol levels.
source: SORT1 encodes a sorting receptor that is expressed in many tissues and has been shown to act in the liver to regulate cholesterol levels (Petersen et al., 1997; Musunuru et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Multiple promoter interactions were identified between SORT1 and the myocardial infarction GWAS locus in CMs.
source: Despite functioning in the liver, we identified multiple promoter interactions between SORT1 and the myocardial infarction GWAS locus in CMs (Figure 7D), directly implicating SORT1 as the target gene and lending further support to experimental validation of this locus as a SORT1 enhancer (Musunuru et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the SORT1 locus.

claim: The ACTA2 gene is located 220 kb away from the heart failure GWAS locus proximal to the CH25H and LIPA genes on chromosome 10q21.
source: Additionally, the ACTA2 gene is located 220 kb away from the heart failure GWAS locus proximal to the CH25H and LIPA genes on chromosome 10q21 (Smith et al., 2010) (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is stated in the results with reference to a figure showing the ACTA2 locus.

claim: ACTA2 encodes the smooth muscle cell-specific actin protein.
source: ACTA2 encodes the smooth muscle cell-specific actin protein and mutations in this gene have been shown to cause coronary artery disease, among other vascular diseases (Guo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Mutations in ACTA2 have been shown to cause coronary artery disease, among other vascular diseases.
source: ACTA2 encodes the smooth muscle cell-specific actin protein and mutations in this gene have been shown to cause coronary artery disease, among other vascular diseases (Guo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the results with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: Chromatin interactions provide an important level of evidence that ACTA2 is a putative causal gene in the development of heart failure.
source: Despite its location at a considerable distance from the GWAS association, chromatin interactions provide an important level of evidence that ACTA2 is a putative causal gene in the development of heart failure.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an interpretation of the chromatin interaction data.

claim: The CM interaction map is useful to interrogate diseases directly related to cardiomyocytes, as in the case of cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Therefore, the CM interaction map is not only useful to interrogate diseases directly related to cardiomyocytes, as in the case of cardiac arrhythmias, but also aids interpretation of target genes that may act in non-cardiac tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: The CM interaction map aids interpretation of target genes that may act in non-cardiac tissues.
source: Therefore, the CM interaction map is not only useful to interrogate diseases directly related to cardiomyocytes, as in the case of cardiac arrhythmias, but also aids interpretation of target genes that may act in non-cardiac tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: Incomplete understanding of long-range gene regulation is a major roadblock in the translation of GWAS-associated loci to disease biology.
source: Incomplete understanding of long-range gene regulation is a major roadblock in the translation of GWAS-associated loci to disease biology.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the problem addressed by the study.

claim: Major challenges in translating GWAS-associated loci to disease biology include identifying putatively causal variants mapping within regulatory elements and functionally connecting these regulatory elements to their target genes.
source: Major challenges in this process include identifying putatively causal variants mapping within regulatory elements and functionally connecting these regulatory elements to their target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the challenges addressed by the study.

claim: High-resolution maps of promoter interactions in human iPSCs and iPSC-derived CMs were generated to delineate gene-regulatory interactions between CVD-associated SNPs and putative causal genes.
source: To delineate gene-regulatory interactions between CVD-associated SNPs and putative causal genes, we generated high-resolution maps of promoter interactions in human iPSCs and iPSC-derived CMs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the study's approach.

claim: Promoters interact with a diverse set of distal DNA elements in both iPSCs and CMs, including known enhancer sequences, which reflect cell identity and correspond to tissue-specific gene expression.
source: We demonstrated that promoters interact with a diverse set of distal DNA elements in both cell types, including known enhancer sequences, which reflect cell identity and correspond to tissue-specific gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: 1,999 CVD-associated SNPs were linked to putative causal target genes using the CM map.
source: To demonstrate the utility of the CM map, we linked 1,999 CVD-associated SNPs to putative causal target genes which identified both validated and potentially novel genes important for cardiovascular disease biology.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The CM map identified both validated and potentially novel genes important for cardiovascular disease biology.
source: To demonstrate the utility of the CM map, we linked 1,999 CVD-associated SNPs to putative causal target genes which identified both validated and potentially novel genes important for cardiovascular disease biology.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Gene regulation by distant regulatory elements involves the bridging of linearly separated DNA sequences through chromatin looping mechanisms.
source: Gene regulation by distant regulatory elements involves the bridging of linearly separated DNA sequences, for example between a promoter and its distal enhancers, through chromatin looping mechanisms (Spitz and Furlong, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a citation supporting the claim.

claim: An enrichment of tissue-defining transcription factor motifs in the distally interacting sequences of differentially expressed promoters provides an important level of evidence to validate the functional relevance of iPSC and CM interactions.
source: In support of this model, we report an enrichment of tissue-defining transcription factor motifs in the distally interacting sequences of differentially expressed promoters both for CMs and iPSCs, providing an important level of evidence to validate the functional relevance of iPSC and CM interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the motif enrichment data.

claim: The interaction maps are high resolution because Hi-C libraries were generated with the 4 bp cutter MboI, which generates fragments with an average size of 422 bp.
source: One explanation for this enrichment is that our interaction maps are high resolution. We generated Hi-C libraries with the 4 bp cutter MboI, which generates fragments with an average size of 422 bp; this increased specificity of the captured region likely leads to better resolution of the underlying enhancer sequence and, consequently, increased power to detect short transcription factor binding motifs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation for the motif enrichment.

claim: Increased specificity of the captured region likely leads to better resolution of the underlying enhancer sequence and, consequently, increased power to detect short transcription factor binding motifs.
source: One explanation for this enrichment is that our interaction maps are high resolution. We generated Hi-C libraries with the 4 bp cutter MboI, which generates fragments with an average size of 422 bp; this increased specificity of the captured region likely leads to better resolution of the underlying enhancer sequence and, consequently, increased power to detect short transcription factor binding motifs.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an explanation for the motif enrichment.

claim: The majority of capture Hi-C studies to date have reported that gene expression level correlates with enrichment for various histone marks.
source: The majority of capture Hi-C studies to date have reported that gene expression level correlates with enrichment for various histone marks.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of previous findings.

claim: Highly expressed genes are more likely to contact active chromatin regions compared to lowly expressed genes.
source: Thus, highly expressed genes are more likely to contact active chromatin regions compared to lowly expressed genes, corresponding to the observed increasing enrichment of contacts and expression we and others have reported.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the histone enrichment data.

claim: Local increase in active or repressive chromatin may be one driving force underlying the expression level-dependent increase in association between promoters and cis-regulatory elements.
source: This local increase in active or repressive chromatin may be one driving force underlying the expression level-dependent increase in association between promoters and cis-regulatory elements, akin to a phase separation-mediated model of enhancer-promoter interactions (Hnisz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed enrichment.

claim: iPSC-derived CMs are known to be relatively immature and do not fully reflect the diverse structural and functional aspects of adult cardiac cells.
source: Although iPSC-derived CMs are known to be relatively immature and do not fully reflect the diverse structural and functional aspects of adult cardiac cells (Gherghiceanu et al., 2011; Karakikes et al., 2015), the difficulty in obtaining pure sub-populations of primary cardiomyocytes with high integrity necessitates the use of an in vitro system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations supporting the claim.

claim: The difficulty in obtaining pure sub-populations of primary cardiomyocytes with high integrity necessitates the use of an in vitro system.
source: Although iPSC-derived CMs are known to be relatively immature and do not fully reflect the diverse structural and functional aspects of adult cardiac cells (Gherghiceanu et al., 2011; Karakikes et al., 2015), the difficulty in obtaining pure sub-populations of primary cardiomyocytes with high integrity necessitates the use of an in vitro system.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a justification for using iPSC-derived CMs.

claim: The CMs used in this study were highly pure and recapitulate known gene regulatory properties of primary cardiomyocytes.
source: We showed that the CMs used in this study were highly pure and recapitulate known gene regulatory properties of primary cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the validation of the CM model.

claim: Nearly 20% of the variants in high LD with CVD associations were assigned to 347 target genes.
source: Because of this purity, we were able to integrate CVD-associated SNPs with CM promoter interactions with high confidence, assigning nearly 20% of the variants in high LD with these associations to 347 target genes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: Target genes were most relevant for GWAS loci associated with cardiac arrhythmias.
source: Supporting the physiological relevance of CMs to the cardiac conduction system, we found that target genes were most relevant for GWAS loci associated with cardiac arrhythmias, in line with previous findings in immune cells that many target gene interactions were unique to relevant immune cell subtypes (Javierre et al., 2016; Mumbach et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: Even for diseases whose etiology involves cell types other than cardiomyocytes, such as myocardial infarction and heart failure, interactions involving loci associated with these diseases were identified that recapitulate the enhancer-promoter interactions in non-cardiac cell types.
source: Our data also revealed that even for diseases whose etiology involves cell types other than cardiomyocytes, such as myocardial infarction and heart failure, we identified interactions involving loci associated with these diseases that recapitulate the enhancer-promoter interactions in non-cardiac cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the GWAS SNP analysis.

claim: A validated myocardial infarction locus interacts with the distal SORT1 promoter in CMs even though this locus has been extensively characterized in the context of cholesterol metabolism in hepatocytes.
source: As an example, we showed that a validated myocardial infarction locus interacts with the distal SORT1 promoter in CMs even though this locus has been extensively characterized in the context of cholesterol metabolism in hepatocytes.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an example of the utility of the CM map.

claim: The promoter interactions linking the disease locus to SORT1 may represent tissue-invariant genome architecture.
source: Therefore, the promoter interactions we observe linking the disease locus to SORT1 may represent tissue-invariant genome architecture, likely reflecting that genome organization in general is relatively stable (Dixon et al., 2015; Jin et al., 2013; Ghavi-Helm et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a speculation about the nature of the SORT1 interactions.

claim: Genome organization in general is relatively stable.
source: Therefore, the promoter interactions we observe linking the disease locus to SORT1 may represent tissue-invariant genome architecture, likely reflecting that genome organization in general is relatively stable (Dixon et al., 2015; Jin et al., 2013; Ghavi-Helm et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations supporting the claim.

claim: Any interaction between a promoter and a putative disease-associated genomic region serves as an important level of evidence to prioritize that gene for future follow-up studies.
source: While we advocate the use of the CM map for investigating gene regulatory mechanisms of diseases related to cardiomyocyte biology, we also emphasize that, where identified, any interaction between a promoter and a putative disease-associated genomic region serves as an important level of evidence to prioritize that gene for future follow-up studies.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a recommendation for using the CM map.

claim: There are likely to be many false negatives, or 'missing' interactions in the PCHi-C maps.
source: The most important caveat is that there are likely to be many false negatives, or 'missing' interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the PCHi-C technique.

claim: The total landscape of promoter contacts in a population of cells is still under-sampled, even with a sequencing depth of ~400M reads per replicate.
source: Although the capture step greatly enriches for promoter-containing ligation fragments in a Hi-C library, the total landscape of promoter contacts in a population of cells is still under-sampled, even with a sequencing depth of ~400M reads per replicate conducted for this study.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the PCHi-C technique.

claim: As the distance between two fragments increases, the read-depth required to robustly identify that interaction also increases.
source: This is due to several factors, including the hybridization efficiency of each bait, ability to design sufficient baits per promoter, and the transient nature of many regulatory interactions. This latter issue is confounded by the distance-dependent effect on ligation frequency: as the distance between two fragments increases, the read-depth required to robustly identify that interaction also increases.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the PCHi-C technique.

claim: CHiCAGO may slightly underestimate the expected number of reads corresponding to intra-TAD interactions which could lead to potential false positives.
source: Additionally, because the CHiCAGO program does not incorporate TAD boundaries into its background model, it may slightly underestimate the expected number of reads corresponding to intra-TAD interactions which could lead to potential false positives.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a limitation of the CHiCAGO program.

claim: There is a strong correspondence between TADs called on pre-capture Hi-C data and PCHi-C interactions identified with CHiCAGO.
source: However, we note that there is a strong correspondence between TADs called on pre-capture Hi-C data and PCHi-C interactions identified with CHiCAGO (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A); this suggests that accounting for TAD boundaries may only marginally improve our ability to identify significant interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a response to the limitation of the CHiCAGO program.

claim: It is possible that long-range interactions may also contribute to gene silencing.
source: A final consideration is the interpretation of interactions involving inactive genes. Although most regulatory elements are thought of as activating, it is possible that long-range interactions may also contribute to gene silencing; this is supported by the observation that silent genes are enriched for long-range interactions to H3K27me3 marked regions (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a consideration for interpreting the data.

claim: Silent genes may contact regulatory elements that are not active in the analyzed cell type or developmental stage.
source: Alternatively, silent genes may contact regulatory elements that are not active in the analyzed cell type or developmental stage; these may represent 'pre-formed' loops between genes and their regulatory elements as characterized in Ghavi-Helm et al. (2014).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an alternative interpretation of interactions involving inactive genes.

claim: The data sets provided represent a highly enriched set of ~350,000 and~400,000 promoter interactions in iPSC and CMs, respectively.
source: Despite these limitations, the data sets we provide here represent a highly enriched set of ~350,000 and~400,000 promoter interactions in iPSC and CMs, respectively; although there are likely missing interactions, the interactions that we did identify should be considered as very high confidence, as they were independently identified in at least two biological replicates and show strong signal of enrichment for known features of genome architecture and gene regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a summary of the data sets provided.

source: Despite these limitations, the data sets we provide here represent a highly enriched set of ~350,000 and~400,000 promoter interactions in iPSC and CMs, respectively; although there are likely missing interactions, the interactions that we did identify should be considered as very high confidence, as they were independently identified in at least two biological replicates and show strong signal of enrichment for known features of genome architecture and gene regulation.

claim: The promoter interaction maps represent important resources for any investigation into the gene regulatory mechanisms underlying cardiovascular disease traits.
source: In conclusion, the promoter interaction maps we generated in this study represent important resources for any investigation into the gene regulatory mechanisms underlying cardiovascular disease traits.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion about the utility of the data sets.

claim: The list of candidate regulatory variants and their target genes may serve as an entry point for several hypotheses related to CVD GWAS, and can be readily tested in experimental settings.

claim: The full set of data presented in this study is hosted as a public track hub at the WashU EpiGenome Browser.
source: To provide both the iPSC and CM maps as an accessible resource, we have hosted the full set of data presented in this study as a public track hub at the WashU EpiGenome Browser (Zhou et al., 2015), accessible at the following link: http://epigenomegateway.wustl.edu/browser/?genome=hg19&publichub=Lindsey.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a description of data availability.

claim: The significant PCHi-C interaction files are provided in the Supplementary Material.
source: Additionally, we provide the significant PCHi-C interaction files used in all analyses in the Supplementary Material (Supplementary files 1 and 2); these can be applied to future multi-omics analyses of gene regulation and disease genetics.
